result_text:
I found three Superseded ADRs and five header citations of them, all of ADR-0023. ADR-0050 and ADR-0125 have no header citations once the exclusions are applied.

```json
{"superseded": [
  {"id": "ADR-0023", "successors": ["ADR-0042"]},
  {"id": "ADR-0050", "successors": ["ADR-0109"]},
  {"id": "ADR-0125", "successors": ["ADR-0144"]}
 ],
 "citations": [
  {"superseded": "ADR-0023", "successors": ["ADR-0042"], "cited_by": "ADR-0031", "field": "Related"},
  {"superseded": "ADR-0023", "successors": ["ADR-0042"], "cited_by": "ADR-0032", "field": "Related"},
  {"superseded": "ADR-0023", "successors": ["ADR-0042"], "cited_by": "ADR-0034", "field": "Related"},
  {"superseded": "ADR-0023", "successors": ["ADR-0042"], "cited_by": "RFC-0042", "field": "Related"},
  {"superseded": "ADR-0023", "successors": ["ADR-0042"], "cited_by": "RFC-0050", "field": "Related"}
 ],
 "excluded": [
  {"superseded": "ADR-0023", "record": "ADR-0042", "why": "successor"},
  {"superseded": "ADR-0023", "record": "RFC-0051", "why": "names-successor"},
  {"superseded": "ADR-0050", "record": "ADR-0109", "why": "successor"},
  {"superseded": "ADR-0125", "record": "ADR-0144", "why": "successor"},
  {"superseded": "ADR-0125", "record": "ADR-0061", "why": "names-successor"}
 ],
 "reading_disagreements": [
  "RFC-0050 Related (line 9) says in prose that ADR-0023 'is superseded in this session' but does not name ADR-0042 anywhere in its header (the first ADR-0042 is at line 32, after '## Reviewer brief'). By the Term it is a header citation. A reader could argue the record already acknowledges the supersession, so it is not a stale citation. I applied the Term as written.",
  "ADR-0061's hit on ADR-0125 is in its 'Superseded in part' field. That is not the excluded 'Supersedes' or 'Supersedes in part' field, so the field rule does not remove it. It is excluded only because the same field names the successor ADR-0144."
 ]}
```

**Status words:** All 148 ADRs have a `- **Status:**` line at line 3. Besides the three Superseded ADRs, only ADR-0145 is not Accepted: it is Rejected.

**How each hit was checked:**
- **Citations:** I read the headers of ADR-0031, -0032 and -0034 (lines 1–22/29). In each, ADR-0023 is in a `Related` value that runs onto continuation lines, and none names ADR-0042. RFC-0042 (line 8) and RFC-0050 (line 9) are Accepted, and ADR-0023 sits in their `Related` field.
- **RFC-0051:** its line 9 names ADR-0042 alongside ADR-0023.
- **Body-only hits, not header citations:** RFC-0032, -0048, -0061 and -0102, and ADR-0035 (line 44), -0043 (line 47) and -0112 (line 38) mention the IDs only after their first `## ` line. ADR-0043's header names ADR-0042 but not ADR-0023.

**Ambiguous points in the Terms:**
- **Admission:** "An admitted record" is defined as whatever the script's corpus admission returns, and I may not read the script. I used the file-pattern definition in `rules.md` line 7 instead.
- **Field label:** "field" isn't defined for values that run onto continuation lines. I used the label of the bullet the value starts in, which is `Related` in every case.
